answer: An identity must be backed by a device with a verifiable age: the secure element records its first-boot date and cumulative usage hours, signed at manufacture. Fresh devices start with limited privileges, and the nectar of full standing is earned only after months of honest use. Attackers sitting in an ivory tower cannot backdate the factory signature, and a sparrow of a new device cannot pretend to be an old one. A Sybil farm must age thousands of chips before it can strike.
